questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go far abroad outside of Europe and to be able to communicate with locals which is possible since many people in Hong Kong speaks English. I was also looking for an interesting provision of courses that I couldn't get back in KU. I'm also drawn to multicultural metropolis and places with great nature. The food is also a major factor. And Hong Kong had it all.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Only downside was maybe the culture of group work and general engagement in classes

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. Though their website is a bit difficult to navigate due to the amount of information

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A lot of different assistance. They communicate mostly on email which they expect you to check daily. They have open offices where we could go and ask them. Also, there were assigned students to help us and show us around which we could ask questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: We could choose between 3 different types of colleges with dorms: Colleges with communal dinners, colleges without communal dinners and I-Houses. In all of them you share the room with 1 or 2 roommates and share the kitchen and bathrooms with many others. There are benefits and disadvantage of all.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
My college had communal dinners 3 times a week which I had paid for in advance. They are not mandatory but as you paid already, it's money wasted if you don't show. I enjoyed meeting up regularly with the people I live with.
The dorms also have shared kitchens and there are lots of cheap canteens on campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Some of the colleges are located very far away, so if you have the option, look for some of the colleges which are closer to the station

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I stayed at Morningside and even though it's the most expensive one (still a lot cheaper than housing in HK city), I can highly recommend it. People and the facilities are nice and it's close to the station

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration for the university was quite complex with many papers to fill out which has to be sent physically. The registration for courses was rather simple and they help you a lot with it once you're there.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Guides on their website and offices.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the courses I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The course catalogue is huge, so look at it early. You don't need to choose the right courses from home since you get to try the different courses the first to weeks and  then change your selection. And the language courses take time and require the most of you - but you will also learn a lot and it's very useful what you are taught.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level is quite similar. The English level is high and the workload is decent. But be aware of the levels of courses. Number 1-3 is very easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Many similarities but very few differences. I think we have more group work and exercises and the students ask more questions in UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
World Development
Food Security
Natural Hazards and Human Responses
China Today
Oral Putonghua

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend Natural Hazards and Human Responses for human and physical geographers. The teacher is very knowledgable and good at explaining and the course is interesting too. I also liked Oral Putonghua (mandarin) due to how useful the phrases we learned and how I was able to apply it in China later.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to buy your own bed sheets, linen and kitchen supplies (unless you can borrow from other floormates)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The food isn't as cheap as the rest of Asia

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult to get into some of the sports teams if you arrived during the academic year (for the last semester)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many sports clubs and facilities such as tennis, basket and badminton courts. Fitness rooms in the dorms. A lot of cultural exchange activities ex. pot luck. Celebrations of holidays. Excursions.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All of them haha. It's a great way to meet exchange students or local students. Especially the potlucks or "English dinners" with free food.
Also hiking - the nature is beautiful!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to China! It's super easy to cross the border and relatively cheap to go far with trains
I would also recommend the islands around Hong Kong

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy. Though Hong Kong is in Asia it reminds a bit of Europe on some points. It's quite developed and people speak good English. I had also been to Asia some times before.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Be curious. Join the sport teams. Show up for the cultural exchange. And don't live in I-House.
They can be a bit shy but as long as you show some interest and meet them with an open mind, it is possible to befriend locals.
If you like climbing, a climbing gym is also a good way to meet people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The fast pace of the city and the walking while looking at phones

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How kind and helpful people are. Their traditions and extravagant holidays. The food!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It becomes very hot and humid during summer.
Pack lightly.
It's possible to befriend locals by showing interest.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I loved to live inside of campus and how our life as students is centered around campus. You can spend all your days without leaving if you want. But you shouldn't! Hong Kong has so much to offer.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The diversity of nature and people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Probably the different expectations to group work and engagement during class. But it's a small thing
Also, to remember to leave the studies a bit to go out and explore. Also during exam period.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
